Created frontend/.env.example with NEXTAUTH_URL, NEXTAUTH_SECRET and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL; API base matches 018's existing localhost:3001 default
Extended the Role union and ENV_BY_ROLE with auth -> DATABASE_URL_AUTH so lockdown tests connect as the real lc_auth role

Created identity_credential with zero lc_app grants, INSERT for lc_identity_writer, SELECT + column-scoped UPDATE(digest,updated_at) for lc_auth. Applied and verified.

Created identity_factor (secret_ciphertext, key_reference, confirmed_at, lockout counters) with zero lc_app grants, plus claim_attempt() SECURITY DEFINER owned by lc_auth applying the FR-020 replay guard across the full 90s window, FR-021 counter and 15-minute lockout in one FOR UPDATE step. PUBLIC execute revoked. Applied and verified.

Created backup_code with set_id grouping, partial index on unconsumed rows, zero lc_app grants, and consume_backup_code() SECURITY DEFINER owned by lc_auth resolving the last-code race under FOR UPDATE
Created session and refresh_token with family lineage, plus resolve_session() (the one function lc_app may EXECUTE) and rotate_refresh() revoking the whole family on detected reuse under FOR UPDATE
Added the unique index on lower(btrim(email)) preceded in the same file by a guard that raises with the duplicate count and addresses; guard verified firing against real duplicates

Ran the duplicate pre-flight against the only existing environment (local dev): found 7 duplicate groups, all test residue from repeated 002 suite runs. Remediated by volume reset; all 36 migrations then applied clean from scratch
Extended the Drizzle schema with the five new tables, a customType bytea for the envelope-encrypted secret, and the identity email expression index
Added the twelve audit actions and their TARGET_ENTITY_BY_ACTION entries, none channel-gated; also added migration 0036 extending the audit_event_action_known CHECK constraint, which T008 had missed
Extended the sanitiser deny-list with code, digest and ciphertext (secret and backup_code were already present) and allowlisted plancode/previousplancode as references rather than data
Recorded the five new tables as deliberately unregistered, in the comment shape identity already uses, explaining that they are protected by grants rather than policies
Unit test for the two Argon2id profiles: distinct, interactive meets OWASP floors, both argon2id, digests self-describe their profile, salting verified
Unit test for the TOTP window: three steps in accepted, every step outside refused, and an explicit test documenting that single-use CANNOT live in the verifier
Unit test for KeyProvider: round-trip, ciphertext never contains plaintext, non-deterministic wrap, cross-key rejected, unavailable key THROWS, tampering rejected, short key refused
Unit test for backup code generation: exactly 10, 130 bits each, no collisions within or across sets, ambiguous characters excluded, zero count refused
Implemented the two Argon2id profiles; neither hasher takes an options argument, which is what makes the profiles unreachable from each other's path
Implemented the otplib wrapper with 30s step and 90s window; epochTolerance is in SECONDS not steps, which the outside-window test exists to catch
Implemented the KeyProvider port with LocalKeyProvider (AES-256-GCM) and KmsKeyProvider; unwrap throws rather than returning falsy
Added assertKeyProviderIsSafe, called from main.ts beside assertApplicationRoleIsSafe: refuses to boot when a deployed environment resolves the local key provider. No override flag
Implemented backup code generation and verifyAgainstSet with a fixed comparison count and no early exit, so the matched code's position is not observable

Integration test for session resolution: live resolves, expired/revoked/unknown all return null indistinguishably, plaintext token never in either table, lc_app denied SELECT but able to EXECUTE resolve_session

Implemented the opaque-token session port (mint, resolve, rotate, revoke) plus the lc_auth Drizzle client; SHA-256 rather than Argon2id because a 256-bit random token has no guessable structure and resolution runs on every request

Implemented SessionGuard - deliberately a Guard, the one place that is right, because Guards run before Interceptors and everything else needs the identity it establishes. Resolves through resolve_session on the lc_app connection, which is why that grant exists
Implemented the per-instance origin throttle, documented in-file as best-effort and NOT authoritative; the per-identity lockout in claim_attempt is the security control

Replaced accept_invitation with the five-argument version as migration 0037 (not 0036 - taken), establishing identity_credential inside the existing transaction. Find-or-create re-keyed from subject to normalized email, which D9 forces
Identity context now takes the identity from the resolved session rather than x-identity-id
Tenant middleware takes the identity from the session while KEEPING x-tenant-id, which was never an identity claim - it names which membership to activate
Acceptance service generates the opaque subject in the product and passes the Argon2id digest as the fifth argument; email and credential moved from headers to the request body
Ran verify:role (4/4) and test:rls (31/31) - both pass unchanged with all five new tables present
Ran test:isolation - 001's suite passes unchanged, 12 files / 70 tests. Authentication precedes tenant selection and did not touch it

THE HARD GATE: as the real lc_app role, SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all five tables is permission denied - not empty; EXECUTE permitted on resolve_session and on nothing else; zero column-level privileges; lc_auth owns nothing; lc_platform and lc_retention reach no material

The D3 regression test: an identity reading its own row through identity_self_row obtains no material, and cannot reach it by join, subquery or EXISTS. Asserts over the actual column list so a future migration adding identity.totp_secret fails here

Acceptance creates identity, membership and credential atomically; a refusal leaves none of the three; a second membership does NOT replace an existing credential; 002's six refusal branches still collapse identically

Both halves of the audit narrowing: lc_auth can insert all twelve with tenant_id NULL and nothing else, lc_app can insert none of them but still writes its own domain actions, and mfa_not_enrolled is absent from the vocabulary entirely

BLOCKING (SC-029): 100% of sign-ins demand a second factor across all six archetypes, 0 complete on a credential alone, 0 sessions before both steps, unenrolled routed to enrollment reaching 0 tenant-scoped resources, challenge token single-use and opaque

Implemented the credential and challenge steps with a single refuse() exit, a dummy Argon2id verification so an unknown email costs the same as a known one, peek-then-consume so a wrong code spends an attempt without burning the challenge, and audit writes for all four actions
Implemented POST /auth/sign-in, /auth/factor and /auth/refresh, each carrying @AuthSurface() and @IdentitySurface() so the ungated status is declared where a reviewer reads it
Wired AuthModule and registered SessionGuard as the one APP_GUARD; taught 004's AuthorizationInterceptor to skip the declared authentication surface

Contract test for POST /auth/sign-in: next=factor with no session, next=enrollment for unenrolled, and the 401 body BYTE-IDENTICAL across unknown email, wrong credential and locked identity; a fresh sign-in supersedes the prior challenge

Rotation and family revocation: reuse revokes the whole family and its sessions, the revocation is not announced, a live access token dies immediately, two simultaneous presentations do not both succeed, and one family's death does not touch another

Lockout: 4 failures then success resets the counter, the 5th locks, a VALID code is refused during the lockout indistinguishably, the credential step is locked too, the lockout lifts on its own, and one identity locking does not affect another

Contract test for POST /auth/factor: exactly one session with a 15-minute expiry, response keys are exactly accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt with no tenant and no archetype, the token actually authenticates, uniform 401 across wrong code / unknown token / replay, and neither token in the database in plaintext

Replay under concurrency: two simultaneous challenges with one valid code yield exactly one success and one session; a used code is refused anywhere in the window; the replay counts as a failed attempt; a different neighbouring-step code still works so the guard is not a blanket; the store holds digests

Key unavailable fails closed: a VALID code is refused when the key is gone, the refusal is byte-identical to a wrong code, nothing leaks about keys or encryption, the failure counts toward the lockout, and restoring the key restores sign-in

The three stand-in headers are gone: 0 src/** files read them (comments stripped so an explanation is not a violation), presenting them buys nothing on tenant-scoped, identity-only or acceptance routes, x-tenant-id STILL works with a real session, and a session cannot be redirected by a header naming another identity

Rewrote the principal unit test for a real session read: the SHAPE is unchanged, the token is presented as a bearer credential, the read is never cached, and an unauthenticated visitor gets an empty principal rather than a throw

Replaced principal.ts with a real session read and DELETED principal.fixture.json. types.ts untouched. Memberships come from 002's route because the session carries no tenant and no archetype (FR-037)
Ran every suite standing on getPrincipal() unchanged: 33 files / 349 tests green across 016a, 018, 019, api-client and the Spanish-copy suites. The seam held - no consumer needed amending
Confirmed git diff over frontend/src/shell, frontend/src/feedback and frontend/src/authz is EMPTY - 016a's module contract survives (FR-048, SC-025)

Component tests for both screens: Spanish copy, NO trusted-device control asserted by several names in both languages, one uniform refusal that leaks no cause, nothing written to browser storage, and keyboard reachability

Implemented the NextAuth v5 Credentials provider whose authorize() calls the API and verifies nothing; no adapter, no session strategy beyond the cookie, and the session callback exposes no token to the client

Implemented the middleware: unauthenticated visitors to private routes go to /ingresar carrying their destination, signed-in visitors on the auth screens go onward, and it forwards x-pathname so the root layout can decide about the shell. Documented in-file as convenience, NOT enforcement
Implemented the sign-in screen in the (auth) route group, outside the shell chrome, with one refusal message whatever the cause and no remember-me control
Implemented the challenge screen over 016a's existing input-otp component, with no trusted-device control of any kind and a route to the backup-code path

Contract test for enrollment begin/confirm: the secret is returned exactly once with no session, an unconfirmed row satisfies no challenge, beginning again discards the prior secret, confirmed_at and mfa_enrolled_at are set together, and an enrolled identity is refused

BLOCKING (SC-029): an INSPECTION test, exhaustive over every key in .env.example and every entitlement in the registry, asserting none is consulted on the enforcement path; plus a codebase-wide scan for any identifier naming such a switch

BLOCKING (SC-029): a dump restored without the key yields 0 working factors (the exact scenario Technical Debt item 11 names), the secret is in no audit entry while the events themselves ARE recorded, and an authenticator app is the only enrollable type
Implemented secret generation, envelope encryption and storage with confirmed_at NULL; beginning again replaces the prior unconfirmed row wholesale

Implemented confirmation setting identity_factor.confirmed_at and identity.mfa_enrolled_at in ONE transaction, since the second is 002/FR-026's shipped interface to the first and they must not diverge
Implemented POST /auth/enrollment/begin and /confirm, reachable only past the credential step with no confirmed factor - the gate is state, not capability
Issued exactly 10 codes inside the SAME transaction as confirmation, stored only as high-entropy-profile Argon2id digests, audited as backup_codes.issued

BLOCKING (SC-029): exactly 10 codes issued once, all stored as irreversible Argon2id digests verified to actually be of those codes, consuming 1 invalidates exactly 1, a consumed code is refused identically to one that never existed, one identity cannot consume another's, no surface returns the set again, and a year's age leaves all 10 valid
Implemented consumption with the fixed comparison count and FOR UPDATE, auditing backup_code.consumed and backup_codes.exhausted as DISTINCT events
A backup code is accepted at the challenge step in place of a generated one, counting toward FR-021's counter so recovery is not an unthrottled bypass

Contract test for recovery: a satisfied challenge emits NO session, remainingCodes only after success, the consumed code cannot be reused, re-enrollment returns a complete new set of 10 plus a session, the previous factor is dead, and abandoning leaves no access
Implemented the backup-code challenge emitting an enrollmentToken and no session, auditing consumption

Implemented forced re-enrollment REUSING the T069/T070 mechanism rather than duplicating it: prepareReenrollment retires the factor, drops the code set and revokes every live session, then EnrollmentService.confirm runs unchanged
Implemented POST /auth/recovery/backup-code and /reenroll, the latter reachable only immediately after a satisfied recovery
Implemented the enrollment screen: a three-stage flow (begin, register with QR URI plus manual key, confirm), nothing persisted to browser storage

Implemented the one-time code presentation with an acknowledgement gate and NO re-display path anywhere in the client - there is no route that returns them, so a view-codes affordance would be a button that cannot work
Implemented the recovery screen, reached from the challenge screen carrying the challenge token, handing straight to re-enrollment because success emits no session
